scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice is the current Company/branch/department-scoped customer account identity and bounded federated history page rendered by the retained customer profile history tab and the /customers API timeline read. The profile summary strip, directory, follow-ups, orders, opportunities, cases, notes, customer portal/attachments, customer authority, Executive evidence consumers and every source-owner command remain retained TypeScript.
scope.domain: Customer 360 read actor policy (commerce.read and selected-context expiry), exact Company and optional branch/department scope, Support history purchase, Field Service module, Finance permission and Legal permission gates, a 1..100 page limit, a scope-bound opaque cursor (Company, branch, department and customer), exact event source/prefix pairs, bounded titles/status/hrefs/versions/timestamps, duplicate rejection and strict descending (at, id) ordering.
scope.application: One customer_timeline use case requires the current actor and Support history entitlement before any source read, validates the customer identity and cursor scope, returns a scoped not-found for an invisible or foreign customer, and derives hasMore/nextCursor only from the requested page plus one overflow row. Every event is validated against its source family before presentation, and a repository row from a disabled source fails closed rather than leaking into the page.
scope.adapters: Read-only PostgreSQL federation over the exact relations already composed by the retained Customer 360 timeline: commerce_orders/commerce_fulfillments/commerce_returns, customer_contact_notes(+history)/customer_followups(+events), crm_leads/crm_opportunities/crm_case_events/crm_lead_activities, support_tickets(+events) with the current IAM assignment predicate, field_service_agreements/orders(+events), finance_invoices and legal_items/legal_native_references/legal_events(+legal_members). It invents no relation or column, performs no write, and requires the caller's serializable Holding transaction. All enabled source queries run inside that one snapshot so the visible customer and event page cannot observe mixed owner states.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/customers/{customer_id}/timeline?cursor=&limit=. Exact registered Host/Holding targets and HTTPS origins, strict customer path shape, strict query keys with duplicate rejection, cursor/limit validation, request-body rejection, private/no-store and no-referrer/nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company scope, Support purchase and serializable owner read.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_CUSTOMER_TIMELINE_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact customer/item/page/context shapes, strict source prefixes, internal-path hrefs, unique ordered IDs, coverage/limitations validation and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader.
scope.ssr: The workplace customer profile history tab uses the native page when ERPX_NATIVE_CUSTOMER_TIMELINE_CONFIG is present. An unset configuration retains customerWorkspaceProfile's timeline. Once configured, an invalid or failed native history read is surfaced through the existing page error policy rather than being silently replaced. The profile summary strip, pending work and notes still use the retained Sales profile read. The feature-sales /customers API route also serves the native timeline for an id query when configured, while an id-less directory read remains retained.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The application requires the current Commercial Support history entitlement through a public port whenever the actor has support.read; a denied purchase hides the Support source without failing the other owners. The legal filter preserves the retained internal/member visibility plus legal_requester request ownership. Finance and Field Service remain permission/module gated. The composition backend must repeat current authority, purchase admission and scope on its own serializable owner transaction.
